title: The Crooked Garden
premise: Paloma Brightwater has spent their whole life in the Valley of Vell, a pocket country erased from every map, where the absence of magic keeps its people invisible to the empire that destroyed them. As a royal food-taster, Paloma builds immunity to poison one dish at a time—until a prophecy book surfaces showing tonight's date, and Paloma's own face beside it. Hunted by an imperial mage who feeds on forgotten nations, Paloma must gather a ragged found family of tasters, thieves, and exiles to find the Crooked Garden: a living door out of Vell that only opens for those willing to pay a memory as toll. In the end, Paloma survives by giving up the valley itself, leading its people through the door into a world where they can finally be seen—at the cost of forgetting the home that made them.
about_author: Odile Voss is the pen name of a former line cook who claims recipes are just spells with worse marketing. They write fantasy about kitchens, borders, and the people history forgets on purpose.

chapters.title: The Taster's Oath
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. A day in the royal kitchens of Vell: swallowing arsenic-laced honey cake, flirting with the archivist Sef, and reciting the taster's oath. Establishes the valley's magicless safety and Paloma's wry loneliness. Emotional beat: contentment built on small, controlled risks.

chapters.title: A Date Written in Ash
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Cataloguing the palace's sealed prophecy room, Sef finds a century-old book whose pages name tonight's date—and a sketch of Paloma at a door made of vines. He brings it to Paloma against protocol. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread.

chapters.title: What the Empire Erased
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The Dowager Queen reveals Vell's truth: it was unmade from maps and memory by imperial magic, surviving only inside its own borders. The prophecy's 'door' is real—the Crooked Garden. Emotional beat: grief for a homeland that was never allowed to exist.

chapters.title: The First Outside Thing
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. An imperial surveyor's drone-like familiar crosses the border—the first magic ever to enter Vell. It marks Paloma with a sigil before Sef burns it out. Emotional beat: the safe world cracking open.

chapters.title: Company of Poisoned Mouths
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV rotation. Paloma recruits fellow tasters: brash Marisol, who tastes lies; old Hobb, immune to everything but regret; and thief-turned-cook Bramble. Emotional beat: reluctant camaraderie forming over a shared death-defying trade.

chapters.title: The Mage Who Eats Countries
chapters.summary: Antagonist POV. Imperial Mage-Censor Ilvane arrives at the border, tasting Vell's absence like vintage wine. She has devoured six forgotten nations and hungers for the seventh. Emotional beat: cold, elegant menace; power as appetite.

chapters.title: Recipes for Vanishing
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The company raids the palace archives for the Garden's location, finding only a cook's ledger from 100 years ago with ingredients that don't exist anymore. Emotional beat: hope requiring archaeology.

chapters.title: Hobb's Confession
chapters.summary: Hobb's POV. Hobb admits he once served Ilvane as her taster and helped her find another nation's door—for immunity, for survival. The price of his survival was everyone else's. Emotional beat: shame, forgiveness, the theme's first hard cost.

chapters.title: Crossing the Salt Fields
chapters.summary: Bramble's POV. The company travels to the valley's edge through salt flats where erased things go to die: ghost-orchards, half-remembered songs. Ilvane's hunters strike; Marisol takes a wound that won't close outside time. Emotional beat: first blood, stakes made flesh.

chapters.title: The Kitchen at the End of the Map
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. They find the ruined waystation kitchen from the ledger and cook its impossible recipe using memories as seasoning. The stove lights without fire. Emotional beat: cooking as communion; found family solidifying.

chapters.title: Ilvane's Offer
chapters.summary: Ilvane's POV. She corners Paloma alone and offers them a place at her table: immortality, immunity, empire—as long as they hand over the prophecy book and let Vell be eaten properly. Emotional beat: temptation framed as mercy.

chapters.title: Refusal, With Garnish
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Paloma refuses—but not nobly; they buy time with a lie about the book's location, hating how easily survival comes. Sef overhears and doubts them. Emotional beat: moral compromise straining the new family.

chapters.title: The Garden Gate
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Guided by the ledger, they reach the Crooked Garden: a hedge-maze grown from the bones of Vell's erased neighbors, its gate sealed by a riddle of courses. Emotional beat: awe shadowed by the graves of those who failed.

chapters.title: Seven Bitter Herbs
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. To open the gate, each member must eat a dish brewed from their worst memory. Hobb relives his betrayal; Marisol nearly drowns in hers. Paloma's dish reveals something they never knew: they were born outside Vell. Emotional beat: vulnerability as the true key.

chapters.title: Born Beyond the Border
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The Dowager Queen confesses: Paloma was smuggled in as an infant from an already-eaten nation—which is why the prophecy names them. Only someone from nowhere can open the door. Emotional beat: identity shattered and remade.

chapters.title: The Siege of Small Country
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Ilvane breaches the valley's edge; magic floods in like water into a hull, and Vell begins unraveling—streets forgetting themselves, people fading. The company defends the Garden gate. Emotional beat: desperate, losing battle.

chapters.title: What Immunity Is For
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Years of swallowed poison have made Paloma the only person who can survive touching Ilvane's raw magic. They realize their whole life of quiet endurance was preparation. Emotional beat: purpose found in the thing they hated most.

chapters.title: The Last Course
chapters.summary: Climax, Paloma's POV. At the gate, Paloma faces Ilvane and serves her a final dish: her own first memory, the nation she came from before she became the empire's mouth. She falters, starving for what she ate. Emotional beat: defeating corruption by feeding it its own humanity.

chapters.title: Toll
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The Garden demands payment: a memory of home. Paloma pays everything—the kitchens, the oath, the taste of honey cake—to hold the door wide enough for all of Vell. Emotional beat: sacrifice as the price of survival, paid willingly.

chapters.title: Through
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. The valley's people pour through the door into the wider world, arriving on a hillside above a real map. Sef holds Paloma, who remembers nothing of Vell but recognizes the feeling of family anyway. Emotional beat: grief and arrival braided together.

chapters.title: A New Book of Prophecies
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Weeks later, in a rented kitchen in a foreign city, Sef finds fresh pages writing themselves in the old prophecy book—new dates, new doors, other forgotten nations still waiting. Emotional beat: the story is bigger than one valley.

chapters.title: First Taste
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Paloma cooks a meal for their ragged family in the new world and, tasting it, feels an echo of a home they cannot name—and chooses to build a new one anyway. Final beat: found family enduring past the price of survival.
